bottleneck: siRNA drugs silence genes with exquisite potency but can also suppress unintended transcripts through partial seed-region matches, causing off-target toxicity that is hard to predict from sequence alone. Delivery beyond the liver relies on conjugates with limited tissue range, and the durability that makes siRNA attractive — months per dose — also makes off-target effects long-lasting and hard to reverse. Designing out seed-mediated off-targets without losing potency remains an unsolved optimization.
current_state: Liver-targeted siRNAs are approved and successful; extrahepatic delivery via antibody and peptide conjugates is in trials but unproven at scale. Specificity screening is improving but incomplete.

title: siRNA off-target silencing with liver-only delivery
why_it_blocks: A silencing drug that hits the wrong gene for months is a liability, not a therapy. Until specificity and delivery broaden together, RNAi's therapeutic footprint stays small despite its elegant mechanism.
